learning_outcomes.text: Acquire theoretical and practical training in surface science and engineering, highlighting its importance in the design and functionality of industrial products.

Understand, modify, and monitor the surfaces of materials (metals, polymers, composites) in relation to their optical, chemical-physical, aesthetic, adhesive, and mechanical properties, such as abrasion resistance.
Evaluate wettability, corrosion phenomena, and material coupling strategies through direct observation of interactions between surfaces and environments.
Select and design surface treatments and adhesion strategies based on the desired surface properties.
Understand how surface properties influence the overall performance of the system.

syllabus_topics: The importance of surfaces in industrial products
Introduction to surface science: surface tension, free energy, interfacial interactions
Aesthetic and optical properties: color, gloss, finish, instrumental measurement
Measurement of wettability and adhesion: contact angle, adhesion models, application examples, and adhesion testing
Methods for modifying surface energy: flame treatment, corona discharge, plasma treatment
Surface preparation and cleaning techniques: degreasing, pickling, conversion treatments
Introduction to corrosion and surface aging: mechanisms, protection strategies, accelerated testing
Application examples on metals, polymers, and hybrid surfaces in various fields, from biomedical applications to design and the transport industry
Laboratory activities: development of a project including the design, fabrication, and characterization of a functional surface prototype
Seminars presenting engineering and industrial application perspectives
teaching_methods: Group-based experimental activities in the laboratory
Preparation of individual or group technical reports
Literature review to identify relevant engineering solutions
Collective presentation and discussion of final reports

assessment_methods.method: Technical laboratory report (including data analysis and presentation)
Written exam complementing the submitted report

assessment_rules: Student performance will be assessed based on their understanding of the course content (50% of the final note) and their ability to apply this knowledge to real-world situations (50% of the final note). The evaluation of the report and its discussion will particularly highlight the applied aspect. The exam type is oral.
